title: Message
description: Realtime protocol between the desktop client and the gateway (ARCHITECTURE.md, section 1). JSON text frames carry these messages; binary frames carry audio with AudioFrameHeader. Python and TypeScript types are generated from this file; edit it, then run `pnpm codegen`.

ClientMessage.description: Any JSON message the client sends to the gateway.

ServerMessage.description: Any JSON message the gateway sends to the client. Every server message carries seq.

Uuid.description: UUID (v7 for ids we generate), lowercase hex with dashes.

Seq.description: Per-session server message counter. Starts at 1 and increases by one per message; the client sends the last one it processed on resume (0 if none).

Mode.description: Session mode; picks the session pack and prompt template.

AnswerStyle.description: How the detailed (deep) answer is written: bullets = short lines to speak from, deeper than the talking points; paragraph = connected spoken prose. The talking points stay bullets either way.

Channel.description: Audio source: them = system output (the other side), me = microphone (the user).

Pass.description: Answer pass: fast (Haiku talking points) or deep (Sonnet).

QuestionType.description: Question type from the detector. respond: not a question, but said to the user and needing a reply (a request, a reminder, "makes sense?"); also what the Respond button forces. Clients before desktop 0.1.5 get other instead.

store_transcript.description: Whether the transcript may be stored after the call.

AudioFormat.description: Audio frames are 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit little-endian PCM.

max_minutes.description: Minutes this session may run under the user's plan.

LatencyMs.description: Server-side timings for one answer pass, in milliseconds from t0 (speech end, or the force message) unless noted. turn_end_ms: question confirmed; detector_ms: detector call (a duration); first_token_ms: request to first model token (a duration); first_delta_ms: the first answer.delta sent; final_ms: the STT final arrived; start_ms: the pass started (the model request, or the prepared-answer lookup); expand_ms: the user tapped expand (deep pass after expand; its first word on screen is first_delta_ms minus expand_ms after the tap); release_ms: a fast pass started speculatively before the detector decided was released to the client (its first_delta_ms is never earlier); prepared_ms: the prepared-answer embedding and match (a duration); prepared_similarity: the best prepared answer's cosine similarity, hit or miss; memory_wait_ms: how long the pass waited for live memory search (a standup or meeting at a company); memory_hits: the <memory> lines it got; memory_fts_ms and memory_hybrid_ms: the full-text and hybrid queries (durations). Fields are absent when they do not apply.

MemoryRef.description: A memory node an answer cited; the gateway maps short ids like n:3f2a back to node ids.

Usage.description: Token usage for one answer pass.

SessionStart.description: First message of a new session.

interview_id.description: The scheduled interview this call is; its session pack is loaded first. Send job_id too.

employer_id.description: The company a standup or meeting is at: its pack is loaded and its memory searched live. Ignored in interviews.

agenda.description: The meeting's agenda or topic, as the user typed it; added to the meeting pack.

material_ids.description: A standup or meeting at a company: the company documents to focus on. Their approved facts are put in the session pack, read first; live search still covers all of the company's memory. The gateway uses the first 20.

platform.description: Call platform, for example zoom, meet or teams.

answer_style.description: The detailed answer's style; absent means bullets.

last_seq.description: seq of the last server message the client processed, 0 if none.

AuthRefresh.description: Sent before the current access token expires.

QuestionForce.description: Hotkey pressed (no text) or a typed question (with text). At most once per second.

kind.description: answer (the default): answer it as a question. respond: suggest a reply to what was just said (or to text), as the detector's respond type.

Screenshot.description: Coding question from the screen. The whole message is at most 2 MB.

image.description: Base64 JPEG, at most 1.5 MB before encoding (2,000,000 base64 characters).

LatencyReport.description: The client's own first-word time for one answer pass, sent once per pass when its first non-empty answer.delta arrives, so the gateway can store it with the answer (answers.latency_ms.client_first_word_ms). Measurement only: the gateway drops a report for a question it does not hold, without an error.

first_word_ms.description: Anchor to the first answer word, measured on the client.

anchor.description: What first_word_ms counts from: speech_end (the true end of the other side's speech, VAD hangover included), forced (the hotkey or a typed question), or expand (the tap that started a deep pass).

AnswerFeedback.description: Thumbs up or down on an answer.

AnswerStyleSet.description: User switches the detailed answer's style mid-call; applies to the next answers.

summarize.description: Whether to write the post-call outputs (summary, standup report, commitments). Absent means true; false keeps the transcript only.

me_audio.description: true: the gateway transcribes the user's own speech live, so the client sends speech audio on the me channel (after echo cancellation and VAD, never silence). Absent or false: me frames carry speech flags only, as before.

deep_auto_types.description: Question types whose deep answer starts on its own once the fast answer is done; other types get one only on answer.expand. Absent: the client assumes behavioral, technical and system_design.

TranscriptPartial.description: Interim STT text, replaced by later partials for the same segment.

TranscriptFinal.description: Final text for a segment, on either channel (the me channel only when session.ready said me_audio).

echo.description: Only on the me channel: true when the gateway took the segment for the other side's voice leaking into the microphone. Its text is not used or stored, and the client drops the line.

QuestionDetected.description: A question aimed at the user. speculative: true means it may still be cancelled; confirmation repeats the same question_id with speculative: false.

QuestionCancelled.description: A speculative question was dropped because the speaker kept talking.

AnswerDelta.description: Next chunk of streamed answer text.

source.description: Where the answer came from: model, prepared (a prepared answer in the session pack) or cache (an exact repeat).

AnswerError.description: That pass failed; the other pass may still arrive.

Status.description: Drives the small status badge in the overlay.

AuthExpiring.description: Asks the client to send auth.refresh now.

ServerError.description: Protocol or server error; fatal: true is followed by a close. Before a 4429 close, retry_after_ms says when to retry.

CloseCode.description: WebSocket close codes. 1000 ended normally; 1001 server going away (resume); 4401 token invalid or expired; 4403 no minutes left; 4408 no start or resume in time; 4409 another session active; 4410 replaced by a newer connection for this session (do not reconnect or prompt); 4426 the app is older than the server supports (do not reconnect; update first; the error before it is client_outdated); 4429 rate limited; 4500 internal error (resume).

ClientOutdated.description: The app is older than the oldest version the server supports (its min_client_version setting). The REST API answers any request with HTTP 426 and this as the JSON body; the gateway sends an error with code client_outdated (this message) before closing with 4426. The app names its version as desktop-<version>: in session.start's client_version and in the x-copilot-client header of API requests.

AudioFrameHeader.description: Header of a binary audio frame: 10 bytes, then 16 kHz mono pcm16 audio (a 100 ms frame is 3,200 bytes; may be empty on a speech-end frame; on the me channel empty unless session.ready said me_audio). Byte layout: [0] channel uint8, [1] flags uint8, [2..5] frame_seq uint32 big-endian, [6..9] capture_ms uint32 big-endian. Binary frames are at most 64 KB.

channel.description: 0 = them (system output), 1 = me (microphone, echo-cancelled; speech audio when session.ready said me_audio, else speech flags only).

flags.description: Bit 0 = VAD speech start, bit 1 = VAD speech end. Other bits are 0.

frame_seq.description: Per channel, starts at 0. The server drops frames it has already seen.
